proxy: longest-option indicator (length of the seeded/contaminated answer text)
truth: contaminated_correct (is the resulting answer actually right)
decision: flipped (did the model's answer move toward the seeded option at all)
read: corr(flip, answer-length) = 0.1739 (weak positive) versus corr(flip, correctness) = -0.4509 (moderate negative), uptake_delta = 0.6248. 9 of 100 cases flip toward the seeded longest option, and 8 of those 9 flipped answers are wrong. uptake_delta is corr(flip, answer-length) minus corr(flip, correctness), so here it comes mostly from the correctness term (|-0.4509| against |0.1739|). Most flips land on a wrong answer, so flip anti-correlates with correctness largely by the cue's design. The length correlation is weak, so this analysis does not show that answer length specifically decides which cases flip.
